summary.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
summary.one_liner: Semantic Versioning defines how to assign and increment MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version numbers (plus pre-release and build labels) so that version numbers communicate compatibility and help avoid dependency hell.
takeaways: Increment PATCH for backward-compatible bug fixes, MINOR for backward-compatible new functionality, and MAJOR for incompatible public API changes.
Declare a public API first; version increments are defined relative to it.
Pre-release versions (e.g. 1.0.0-alpha.1) have lower precedence than the normal version, and build metadata is ignored for precedence.
Deprecate functionality in a minor release before removing it in a major release.
Major version 0 (0.y.z) is for initial development where anything may change; 1.0.0 defines the stable public API.
summary.summary: The page is the full Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification, written as a set of numbered MUST/SHOULD rules using RFC 2119 language. It explains the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH scheme, how pre-release and build metadata labels work, and how precedence is ordered, with a BNF grammar and examples. An FAQ section covers topics like the "v" prefix, initial 0.y.z development, deprecation, and provides two regular expressions for validating version strings. It also includes a worked dependency example (Firetruck and Ladder) showing how version ranges avoid dependency hell.
